answer:
The Slack thread claim that the Teams integration is "basically done" is incorrect and is contradicted by the authoritative roadmap. The authoritative status is that the Microsoft Teams integration is **under active design and planning**, with a release target of Q4 2026 (v2.11.0, November release), and is not generally available [NL-014#NL-014-S07].

The Slack thread itself is explicitly classified as an informal, low-authority internal developer discussion that does not constitute official product documentation; it explicitly defers to the Product Roadmap (`NL-014`) for official timelines [NL-027#NL-027-S01]. Within that thread, the CTO clarifies the integration is slated for *design* in Q4 2026 and that they are not actively writing code for it [NL-027#NL-027-S03]. The Product lead reiterates that the integration is in design for Q4 and that the roadmap remains the source of truth [NL-027#NL-027-S04].

Furthermore, the sales claim that the integration is "basically right around the corner" is flagged as a "significant sales overclaim" because the official roadmap states it is 'in design / planned for Q4 2026' and not generally available [NL-023#NL-023-S04]. The engineering resource debate also confirms that the Teams integration will stay in the design phase for Q4, with development slated for early 2027 [NL-015#NL-015-S06]. Currently, only the Slack connector is available as a limited pilot for select Growth and Enterprise customers [NL-014#NL-014-S07].
